different potato cultivars viz.  S e k u r a ,
Zhukovskij Rannij, Vega and Red Scarlett with
preliminary symptoms of wilt disease were
sampled for Fusarium spp. isolation. To obtain
isolates root necks of diseased plants were
surface sterilized in 0.5% sodium hypochlorite
for 2 minutes with successive thorough rinsing
in sterile distilled water, and then transferred
onto sterile Potato Dextrose Agar (PDA) and
Czapek Dox Agar (CDA) supplemented with 50
mg/L chloramphenicol to inhibit bacterial
growth. Pure Fusarium  i s o l a t e s  w e r e
transferred onto fresh sterile PDA, with
subsequent incubation at 25±2°C for 7 days
under 12 hr alternating light (black/white).
Obtained fungi were identified as Fusarium
isolates based on their macro and microscopic
morphology. For species identification, the DNA
of the isolates was isolated by the phenol-
chloroform method and used for the
amplification of the 5.8S rRNA gene: conserved
regions (internal transcribed spacer) using the
primers ITS1 (TCCGTAGGTGAACCTGCGG),
ITS4 (TCCTCCGCTTATTGATA TGC).
The pathogenicity of the isolates was
assessed by their ability to cause FDR when
artificially inoculated into tubers with fungal
spores. Using a micro-syringe, 20 µL of fungal
spore suspension (105/ml) was inoculated into
each of 10 tubers of the cultivars Zhukovskij
Rannij, Red Scarlet and Reggi. Tubers
inoculated with normal sterile saline were
used as negative controls. Wounded tubers
were rapped separately in sterile filter papers,
placed in sterile labelled paper bags, and
incubated in a humid chamber at 25°C for 21
days. After a continuous incubation of 7 days,
tubers were then checked daily for external
signs of dry rot disease until the 21 st day of
incubation. Following 21 days of incubation,
the number of days until the appearance of
FDR symptoms was recorded for each isolate.
Tubers were then cut across the wound, the
coverage of FDR was measured, and the tuber
resistance was scored based on an inverse
proportion of affected tuber tissue using a 9-
point scale: where 9 is the absence of damage
to the tuber tissue (completely resistant), and
7, 5, 3 and 1 correspond to lesions of 1–25, 25–
50, 50–75 and 75–100% of tuber tissue,
respectively (Bomok, 2019). Cultivar
resistance indices [CRI] were determined using
following Equation 1.
TH –TA
CRI = ––––––––––––– (Eq. 1)
TH
Where, T H a nd T A r ep r es en t  t he s c or e s  of
healthy and affected tubers for that particular
cultivar, respectively. In this case, if 1  CRI >
0, the cultivar was concluded to be resistant,
while a cultivar was characterized as
susceptible if 0 > CRI  -1.
To confirm Koch’s postulates, the BOX-
and ERIC-PCR methods, which are used for
DNA fingerprinting in bacteria and fungi were
carried out to compare the original and re-
isolated pathogenic Fusarium spp. (Mishra et
al., 2015).
The scores of tuber resistance were
subjected to a normal distribution test, and a
Kruskal-Wallis (H) test to assess the influence
of cultivar type on the manifestation of FDR
using the SPSS software version 25.0, taking
into account all replicates per treatment.
RESULTS  AND  DISCUSSION
Fungal Isolation and Molecular Identification
A total of 14 fungal isolates belonging
to the genus Fusarium were obtained from the
root necks of sampled wilting potato plants. Five
isolates Fusarium spp. were obtained from the
plants of the Sekura cultivar, in some
instances, two isolates were isolated from one
plant. Three isolates each were obtained from
varieties Zhukovskij rannij, Vega and Red
Scarlett, respectively. All sequence data
exhibited between 97 to 100% homology among
the tested isolates. The isolate AM9 was
identified as F. solani , while the remaining
thirteen were identified as F. oxysporum. All
obtained sequenced data have been uploaded
into the NCBI Genebank under accession
numbers provided in Table 1. Similar to these
results, F. oxysporum  was confirmed as the
most common potato wilt-associated pathogen
in Tunisia (Ayed et al., 2006). This species was
ranked the leading cause of dry rot in seed
potato tubers in Michigan, USA (Gachango et
al., 2012). Thus, being the dominant party
among isolates, F. oxysporum could present a
greater threat to potato production in the
middle Volga Region.
50 Akosah, Vologin, Lutfullin, Hadieva, Scyganova, Zamalieva and Mardanova
